messages.author: 722521532a54784f
messages.subject: Allele balance
parts:
Hi,
I have read that you can also filter for allele balance to eliminate false heterozygous (see OLeary et al., 2018. These aren’t the loci you’re looking for- Principles of effective SNP filtering for molecular ecologists: https://doi.org/10.1111/mec.14792):

"Allele Balance compares the number of reads for the reference allele to the number of reads for the alternate allele across heterozygotes. The expected allele balance is 0.5; large deviations may indicate false heterozygotes due to coverage effects, multilocus contigs or other artefacts."

At the moment in dartR, there is no function that does this, correct?

I guess this would mean calculating a ratio between AvgCountRef & AvgCountSnp for all heterozygous loci?

Thank you for any feedback on this.
Best,
Gabriella

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Allele balance
parts:
Hi Gabriella,

From what I understand is that the allele balance is calculated for each genotype. AvgCountRef & AvgCountSnp are the number of reads across all samples. So, we cannot calculate the allele balance from the information provided in DArT’s report. The good news is that we are working with DArT to access the raw data from their servers through dartR. Then we will be able to calculate the allele balance and much other exciting information. However, this process will take a couple of months more.

In the meantime, another filter you could use to identify this type of genotyping error would be gl.report.hwe and filter them out with gl.filter.hwe. 

Cheers,
Luis
